signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: CAD/JPY is the primary G10 theme of the week as the Loonie outperforms peers by 0.760% while the Yen lags at -0.798%, creating a significant 1.557% spread. This divergence is fundamentally supported by a 125bp OIS carry advantage for CAD (CORRA 2.28% vs TONA 0.98%) and a resilient ESI of +12.0 for Canada. While JPY bond yields are rising on hike expectations, the current G10 flow heavily favors the CAD's carry-plus-data profile. USD/CAD technicals confirm broader CAD strength, with price at 1.3930 holding below the SMA20/50 cluster at 1.4038/1.4074, signaling a sustained shift in momentum. The bilateral spread well exceeds the 1.20% critical threshold, marking this as the dominant institutional regime. Trade bias: Long CAD/JPY; strong G10 bilateral divergence supported by positive CAD data surprises. Catalyst: BoC meeting 9 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: Unexpected JPY intervention or a sharp move in US CPI that forces a broad carry unwind.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Positioning vs Options Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.37, holding below its SMA20/50 cluster near 161.00 but above the long-term SMA200 at 158.12. COT data shows leverage funds are net short JPY at -63,633 contracts, maintaining a crowded carry trade supported by the 275bp Fed-BoJ spread. However, the options market is pricing in significant tail-risk, with 25d Risk Reversals at -2.19, indicating a strong preference for Yen calls (USD/JPY puts). This creates a sharp divergence: speculators are positioned for carry persistence while options markets are hedging for a downside breakout. With VRP at -1.5%, implied volatility is trading below realized, suggesting the market is underpricing the potential for a volatile breakout as price tests the 160.00 psychological level. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY; options skew warns of a positioning unwind despite the carry advantage. Catalyst: US CPI release. Risk: Continued verbal intervention from Japanese authorities triggers a liquidation of spec shorts.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Hawkish RBA vs Positioning Extreme
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7060, currently positioned above its SMA20, 50, and 200 cluster (0.6931-0.7013), confirming a bullish technical regime. The RBA at 4.35% provides a -60bp carry advantage over the USD in OIS terms, and the real rate of +0.60% is now more restrictive than several G10 peers. CFTC data shows speculators are heavily long AUD at 72.1%, while retail sentiment has reached a 76% short extreme. This institutional versus retail divergence at a technical ceiling suggests a squeeze if US CPI data underwhelms. OCBC research aligns with this constructive outlook, citing the hawkish RBA stance as a primary support pillar for the currency. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD; retail fade of institutional length provides fuel for a trend extension. Catalyst: US CPI next week. Risk: Commodity price weakness drags AUD lower, invalidating the carry-driven bid.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Volatility Risk Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD remains flat near 1.3508, yet the options market is pricing in substantial uncertainty ahead of upcoming macro catalysts. The 1M implied volatility at 11.0% vs a realized 30-day volatility of 6.0% creates a significant +5.0% Volatility Risk Premium (VRP). This suggests traders are paying a heavy premium for protection despite the pair's range-bound price action above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3368-1.3425). COT positioning remains net long at +39,039, though the 25d Risk Reversal shows a mild -0.47 put skew, indicating that even with institutional length, the bias is toward hedging downside shocks. The neutral 0bp carry differential (Fed 3.75% vs BoE 3.75%) leaves the pair primarily sensitive to data surprises rather than structural yield flows. Trade bias: Neutral/range GBP/USD; high vol premium makes directional bets expensive. Catalyst: US CPI release today. Risk: A clean break of the 1.3425 SMA20 support level.
